commits.message:
fix(renderer): a wall stepped back moves every held instant back with it, and the wake is declared first and decided in its slot (883)

- The renderer sees a step back as a turn's instant earlier than the last,
  and its held deferrals, menu idle periods and feed instants all move back
  by it; feeds lose their own step-back branches. A wall gone forward moves
  nothing: it is what a machine that slept looks like.
- The wake takes each declaration before any other taker, so a throw there
  cannot leave the renderer's one timer unarmed.
- A due's declaration carries its failure: the hold-off and its line are
  decided in the due's slot, and the wake's own path handles only a due no
  renderer answered.
- A watched session's request from a pane shown otherwise announces its
  viewers, and every join is stamped on them, so a subscriber that takes
  another's place is owed a frame.
- A stale comment on how a tmux subscription is admitted is corrected.

fix(renderer): the wake times its dues on the monotonic clock, and a host fault after a turn's landing no longer swallows its effect-done (883)

- A due's wait is armed from the wall once, then timed on the monotonic
  clock to the whole millisecond at or after its instant, and handed in at
  its slot's instant like every input: a wall stepped back delays no due,
  and no input runs at an instant earlier than a turn ahead of it.
- A due that threw holds off every declaration after it until a due
  answers, and a due no renderer answered re-arms the last declaration.
- The instant already armed keeps its timer.
- A feed woken after the wall stepped back draws at once, as `due` does.
- A click makes no menu-idle record: only draws do, and retirement ends them.
- Taking a turn's declarations and frames after its changes landed cannot
  fail the turn: a throw there is the host's fault, on every bar.
- A push nobody awaits writes its turn line with what it cost.
- tmux's poll announces only a view that changed.
- Viewers turns close with the wake, first in the teardown.
- The crossing reaches keep their effects-at-boundaries exception marker;
  a stale comment and memory lines are brought in line.

feat(renderer): time is handed in: the renderer owns animation, the menu idle close and pushed frames, and the draw writes nothing (883)

The renderer reads no clock. Each turn carries its instant, and every output
declares the earliest instant the renderer wants a turn at; the host keeps one
timer to that declaration and hands in a `due` through the mailbox, ordered
against every other input. Feeds' cadence, the menu idle close and the
catch-up reload walk all run as due turns. The host keeps who watches and
what each subscriber was sent, and announces a change to its viewers only once
the change is whole.

chore(release): set `package.json` to 1.227.0
